title: 上を向いて歩こう (Ue wo Muite Arukō — I Look Up as I Walk)
description:
The most internationally famous Japanese song ever recorded. Written in 1961 by lyricist 永六輔 (Ei Rokusuke) and composer 中村八大 (Nakamura Hachidai), and performed by 坂本九 (Sakamoto Kyu), it reached #1 on the US Billboard Hot 100 in June 1963 — the only Japanese-language song ever to do so. American radio stations called it 'Sukiyaki' because the real title was too hard to pronounce. The song was reportedly inspired by 永六輔's grief following the 1960 Anpo Struggle (anti-US Security Treaty protests).

The lyrics describe someone walking alone at night through different seasons (spring, summer, autumn), looking upward so tears will not fall. The emotional restraint and bittersweet tone are characteristically Japanese.

For learners: This is excellent N4–N5 material with simple, clear vocabulary, slow tempo, and very deliberate pronunciation by Sakamoto Kyu. Key words: 上を向いて (looking upward), 涙がこぼれないように (so that tears won't spill), 思い出す (to remember), 一人ぽっちの夜 (a lonely night), にじんだ星 (blurring/smearing stars), 幸せ (happiness), 雲の上に (above the clouds), 悲しみ (sadness), 星のかげに (in the shadow of the stars), 泣きながら歩く (walking while crying).
